To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
dopamine acting via D2 receptors is an important regulator of the melatonin biosynthetic enzyme NAT in the chicken retina.
dopamine, acting through D2‐receptos, is involved in the regulation of the cyclic AMP‐mediated dark‐evoked rise in NAT activity in chicken retinal photoreceptor cells.
dopamine D2‐dodopaminergic neurotransmitters are involved in the inhibition of the melatonin‐synthetizing enzyme, serotonin N‐acetytransferase (N‐AT), in chicken retina by light.

the effects of drugs affecting dopamine receptors and of drugs affecting phosphodiesterase activity on melatonin synthesis.

the cyclic AMP‐mediated activation of the melatonin synthesis in chicken retina is regulated via dopamine receptors.
